classification.habitat: Riverbanks, moist areas and tropical/subtropical woodland

identification.description: Deciduous tree with characteristic trifoliate leaves and showy flowers.
identification.whole_plant: Small to medium tree with spreading crown.
identification.leaf: Trifoliate leaves with three leaflets arising from a common petiole.
identification.flower: Showy flowers with numerous prominent stamens, often white to yellowish with changing colour tones.
identification.seed: Numerous seeds embedded in fleshy fruit.
identification.bark: Grey-brown bark; stem bark is the principal traditional drug part.

therapeutics.precautions: Use authenticated stem bark and avoid equating traditional stone-related use with guaranteed stone dissolution.

reference_hubs: TDU Indian Medicinal Plants Database — Shlokas

major_constituents: Flavonoid and triterpenoid constituents reported from bark studies
phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Composition depends on plant part and extraction.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Crataeva nurvala has been investigated for urinary and phytochemical properties; evidence should be interpreted by preparation and study design.
modern_information.safety_notes: Urinary obstruction or suspected stones require appropriate clinical assessment; do not substitute herbal use for evaluation of acute symptoms.

exam_points: Trifoliate leaves are a key identification character
viva_questions: Which part of Varuna is commonly used?
What is a distinctive leaf character?
mnemonics: VARUNA = three leaflets + urinary traditional use
student.quick_revision: Varuna — Crataeva nurvala — Capparaceae — stem bark — Mutrala/Ashmaribhedana.

teaching_points: Demonstrate trifoliate leaf and flower morphology

doctor.quick_reference: Stem bark traditionally used in urinary and Ashmari-related presentations.
key_precautions: Do not delay evaluation of urinary obstruction
